newsitem.title: USA: FDIC agrees to less frequent visits to small banks.
newsitem.headline: FDIC agrees to less frequent visits to small banks.

text.p: Federal Deposit Insurance Corp adopted an interim rule Tuesday allowing for less frequent inspections of small banks in good financial condition.

Generally, bank regulators must examine each bank every 12 months. But banks with less than $100 million in assets that rated "oustanding" at their last exam had to be checked on only every 18 months.
Under the rule adopted at an open board meeting Tuesday, the $100 million exemption ceiling was raised to $250 million.
The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Office of Thrift Supervision will also implement the interim rule, the FDIC said.
About 1,087 more financial institutions will qualify for less frequent examinations under the interim rule, FDIC said.
The agency asked for comments on how the rule should apply to U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks.
